issues.description: The function simulate_msd_two_rounds is specified in the problem statement to accept a batch_size parameter (simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float]). The template implementation, however, defines simulate_msd_two_rounds without a batch_size parameter (def simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots:int, p: float) -> tuple[float, float]:) while its docstring mentions batch_size. The solution implementation includes the batch_size parameter in the signature. This mismatch (problem ↔ template ↔ solution) will confuse students and can cause runtime errors if tests or later code call the function with a batch_size argument or expect batching behavior described in the docstring.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the template function signature to include the batch_size parameter (with the same default) so it matches the problem specification and the solution. For example: def simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float]:. Also ensure the template docstring and any tests assume the same signature.
